advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Put the outside argument in 'mixed-in-and-out' on the repo's drive (D:), so that dropping the under-cwd early return would produce a pin and fail the test
evidence: tests/_nested_pytest.py:118-121: `return ["--rootdir", pathmod.commonpath(dirs)]` / `except ValueError:  # arguments on different drives ... return []`
tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:239: the existing 'two-drives' case already shows that C:+E: arguments give [] through the ValueError path
advisory.finding: The new 'mixed-in-and-out' case does not test the 'any argument under cwd leaves the pin out' rule. Its outside path is on C: and its inside path is on D:. If the `_is_within` early return were removed or broken, `commonpath` would raise ValueError on the two drives and the function would still return [], so the case passes for the wrong reason, just like the 'two-drives' case.
scenarios: Someone changes _rootdir_pin to skip under-cwd arguments (`continue`) instead of returning [], and mixed-in-and-out still passes because the C:/D: commonpath raises ValueError
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a same-drive outside path to _WIN_EXISTING (e.g. "D:\\tmp\\t1" and "D:\\tmp\\t1\\test_y.py") and use `["D:\\tmp\\t1\\test_y.py", f"{_WIN_REPO}\\tests\\test_x.py"]` for mixed-in-and-out. Without the early return, commonpath would give "D:\\" and the test would fail.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the case-change guard exercise the fake's under-cwd (startswith) branch, e.g. assert that a case-changed under-cwd path combined with an outside path gives a result only possible if the under-cwd path was seen as existing, or assert the fake's exists() on the under-cwd-case path directly.
evidence: tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:212: """Guards the fake above: the case-changed under-cwd argument must reach ``_is_within``."""

tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:190-191: the fake has two branches: `ntpath.normcase(p) in {ntpath.normcase(e) for e in _WIN_EXISTING}` or `ntpath.normcase(p).startswith(ntpath.normcase(_WIN_REPO))`. The new test only exercises the first.
tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:230: under-cwd-case argument 'd:\A\Rebar\rebar\tests\unit\test_x.py' is not in _WIN_EXISTING, so it relies only on the startswith branch

tests/_nested_pytest.py:111: `if arg.startswith("-") or not pathmod.isabs(path) or not exists(path): continue`. A missing path is skipped and the function ends at `if not dirs: return []` (line 116-117), the same [] the under-cwd-case parameter expects.

Named violating input: change the fake's second branch back to `p.startswith(_WIN_REPO)`. Then `_win_pin(["-q", "d:\\A\\Rebar\\rebar\\tests\\unit\\test_x.py"])` still returns [] (the path is skipped as missing), and test_a_case_changed_argument_still_counts_as_existing still passes.
advisory.finding: The new guard test claims to protect the case-changed *under-cwd* argument, but it passes an outside-cwd argument. That argument only reaches the fake's `_WIN_EXISTING` membership branch, never the `startswith(normcase(_WIN_REPO))` branch that the under-cwd-case argument depends on. If that branch regressed to comparing case exactly, under-cwd-case would again return [] because the path reads as missing, and no test would notice.
scenarios: Someone later simplifies the `_win_pin` fake and the case-insensitive prefix check goes back to comparing case exactly. Every test stays green, but under-cwd-case has stopped testing `_is_within`'s normcase. That is the exact problem this commit fixes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case-changed under-cwd path to the guard. One option: assert `_win_pin([_WIN_TEST, "d:\\A\\Rebar\\rebar\\tests\\unit\\test_x.py"]) == []` alongside `_win_pin([_WIN_TEST]) == ["--rootdir", _WIN_DIR]`. Both paths are absolute, so with the outside argument alone the pin appears, and with the case-changed under-cwd argument added it returns [] only if that argument was seen as existing and matched by `_is_within`. Or fix the docstring so it says the test covers only the `_WIN_EXISTING` branch.
